name: Aarhus University
about: Aarhus is Denmark's second university and second city, with roughly 38,000 students and a park campus of yellow-brick buildings that runs right into the middle of town. Almost everything it teaches at bachelor level is in Danish; six degrees are taught in English, four of them in Aarhus itself, one in the small town of Herning an hour west, and all of them in computing, economics or cognitive science. AU is also unusually explicit about the numbers: every programme page publishes last year's quota 1 cut-off, the standby cut-off and the admission area number.
ibNotes: AU requires an IB Diploma with a minimum of 24 points. Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results or an IB Certificate of at least 18 points with grade 3 or above in every subject qualify only in combination with supplementary courses (at least two subjects, at least one at A level and one at B level, taught in Danish at VUC/GSK) or a later full IB Diploma.

AU's IB results-service institution code is 000150. AU says: "You must inform your IB-coordinator to register you at IBNETs 'result service' if you earn your IB diploma in the year of application." AU knows your diploma arrives after the 5 July documentation deadline, which is why online access matters more than uploads — get a receipt for the registration.

The application deadline is 15 March at 12.00 noon for IB holders "regardless of whether you apply for admission in quota 1 or 2 or if you earn your IB diploma in the year of application". This is earlier than the 5 July deadline that applies to Danish-exam holders.

AU publishes its own additions to the Ministry's subject conversion: Global Politics HL counts as Social Science B; Global Politics SL counts as Social Science B only in combination with Economics SL or HL; Pre-IB subjects and IB MYP5 subjects count as C level only.

For the Danish A requirement (which no English-taught programme has, but which matters if you also apply to Danish-taught programmes): Danish/Norwegian/Swedish A or A Literature at HL or SL counts as Danish A, and Danish/Norwegian/Swedish B HL counts as Danish A only in combination with English A. Danish B at SL is not accepted.
AU states plainly that there is no dispensation from the English language requirement if English is not a subject on your IB Diploma.

Non-EU/EEA fee-paying applicants effectively cannot apply straight out of the IB: "if you are a paying applicant, then you cannot apply if you earn your IB exam in the year of application as the documentation deadline for paying applicants is 15 March at 12:00 noon."
quotaNotes: You do not choose a quota at AU. All international applicants are assessed in quota 2 automatically, and also in quota 1 if their qualifying exam converts — an IB Diploma does. Quota 1 is a straight ranking on the converted GPA of your first completed qualifying examination, and the last person admitted sets that year's cut-off, published on 28 July. Supplementary courses can fix a missing subject level but their grades never count in quota 1. Quota 2 for the English-taught programmes is an overall assessment of two things: your grade point average in a named list of "particularly relevant quota 2 subjects" for that programme, and documented relevant qualifications, which AU says can add 0.4, 1.0, 1.5 or more to your quota 2 GPA. Everything counted in quota 2 must be completed and documented by 15 March. Separately, most AU programmes have a standby list: you tick standby when you apply, and a standby offer means you may still be offered a place up to mid-August, or otherwise get preapproved admission to the same programme the following year. AU publishes the standby cut-off alongside the quota 1 cut-off, and it is often a point or more lower.

deadlines.label: Application (all international applicants, including IB) — quota 1 and quota 2
deadlines.notes: Also the deadline for documenting everything you want counted in the quota 2 assessment, for the application fee if you are a paying applicant, and for sending in your signed signature page. The application system opens 1 February.

deadlines.label: Special educational support application (early admission)
deadlines.notes: You must still have applied on optagelse.dk by 15 March.

deadlines.label: Answer for paying (non-EU/EEA) applicants
deadlines.notes: Paying applicants are answered early so they can start the residence permit process. Some qualified paying applicants are told on 1 June that they were not strong enough for early admission and are answered again on 28 July.

deadlines.label: Documentation of your qualifying examination; application for a standby place
deadlines.notes: AU: "The deadline for applying for standby is 5 July at 12.00 noon." IB candidates finishing in May 2027 will not have a paper diploma by this date, which is why the IBIS results-service registration is essential.

deadlines.label: Answer to your application and publication of quota 1 cut-offs
deadlines.notes: Available study places for the second-round intake are announced the same day.

deadlines.label: Deadline for confirming your study place

tuitionNonEu: Academic year 2026/2027, per year (60 ECTS): EUR 13,000 for Cognitive Science and for Economics and Business Administration in both Aarhus and Herning; EUR 17,300 for Computer Science, Data Science and IT Product Development. Application fee EUR 150 (DKK 1,125) per applicant, payable by 15 March and refunded only if you enrol and are still enrolled on 1 October. AU states: "Aarhus University does not offer scholarships for any of our Bachelor's degree programmes." EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay nothing.

notes: A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. AU repeats this on each programme page: "B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade."

AU attaches a converted-GPA floor to quota 1 on five of the six English-taught programmes: you need at least 6.0 on the Danish 7-point scale in your qualifying examination to be assessed in quota 1 at all. Below that, your application can only go through quota 2. Economics and Business Administration in Herning does not state such a floor.
Computer Science, Data Science and IT Product Development add a second floor: a minimum GPA of 6.0 in Mathematics A specifically, on top of the overall 6.0.
The 6.0 floor is not the cut-off. The cut-off is what the last admitted applicant actually scored, and in 2026 that was 11.4 for Computer Science and 11.2 for Data Science.

AU tells Danish applicants to treat the English-taught Computer Science, Data Science and IT Product Development degrees as the harder route and to apply to the Danish-taught equivalents (Datalogi, Datavidenskab, It-produktudvikling) as well. For Data Science AU says outright that the English version "is intended for international students". The two versions lead to the same English-taught master's.

The standby cut-off is published next to the quota 1 cut-off and is usually lower — dramatically so for IT Product Development in 2026 (10.1 in quota 1, 6.9 for standby). You have to tick standby when you apply, and the standby application deadline is 5 July.

Herning is not Aarhus. AU Herning is a small campus roughly an hour west of Aarhus in a town of about 50,000, running a few business, engineering and technology programmes. Its Economics and Business Administration degree is academically similar to the Aarhus one but had a 2026 cut-off of 6.9 against 9.2.

Non-EU/EEA students should read the paying-applicant rule before anything else: the 15 March documentation deadline means you cannot be assessed on results you receive in July, so a May 2027 IB candidate who is a paying applicant would need to apply a year later.

programmes.name: Cognitive Science
programmes.summary: The study of how minds work, done with data rather than argument: you learn statistics and programming early and use them to run your own experiments on behaviour, language and the brain. Lab work includes brain scans, behavioural experiments and large text databases. It is housed in the Faculty of Arts but it is a quantitative degree, and you will be writing code in your first year.
programmes.requirementsText: Specific admission requirements: You must fulfil the following specific admission requirements: English B. Mathematics B. History B or History of Ideas B or Social Studies B or Contemporary History B. B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade. Grade point Average (GPA) requirement of 6.0 in quota 1: You must have a minimum GPA of 6.0 on the Danish 7-point grading scale in your qualifying examination to be assessed in quota 1.
extraRequirements: Converted-GPA floor of 6.0 to be assessed in quota 1 at all.
Standby cut-off 2026: 10.5.
Quota 2 subjects (the ones whose grades form your quota 2 average): English B, Mathematics B, and History B or History of Ideas B or Social Studies B or Contemporary History B.
Admission area number on optagelse.dk: 22419. Teaching starts in week 35.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.summary: A theory-solid computer science degree — algorithms, systems, security, software design — aimed at people who want to build apps, cloud services and IT systems and understand why they behave as they do. It is the most competitive English-taught bachelor at AU on 2026 figures. Expect mathematics to be a working tool throughout, not a first-year hurdle.
programmes.requirementsText: Specific admission requirements: You must fulfil the following specific admission requirements: English B. Mathematics A. B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade. Grade point Average (GPA) requirement of 6.0 in quota 1: You must have a minimum GPA of 6.0 and a minimum GPA of 6.0 in Mathematics A on the Danish 7-point grading scale in your qualifying examination to be assessed in quota 1.
extraRequirements: Two separate quota 1 floors: an overall converted GPA of 6.0 and a grade of at least 6.0 in Mathematics A.
Standby cut-off 2026: 10.5.
Quota 2 subjects: English B and Mathematics A.
Admission area number on optagelse.dk: 22112.
AU advises Danish applicants to also apply for the Danish-taught Datalogi, because the English-taught programme has limited spots.

programmes.name: Data Science
programmes.summary: Mathematics, statistics and programming aimed squarely at getting reliable answers out of very large datasets. It sits between computer science and statistics and is the right choice if the appeal is the analysis rather than the systems engineering. AU states that the English-taught version is intended for international students and that it is academically equivalent to the Danish-taught Datavidenskab.
programmes.requirementsText: Specific admission requirements: You must fulfil the following specific admission requirements: English B. Mathematics A. B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade. Grade point Average (GPA) requirement of 6.0 in quota 1: You must have a minimum GPA of 6.0 and a minimum GPA of 6.0 in Mathematics A on the Danish 7-point grading scale in your qualifying examination to be assessed in quota 1.
extraRequirements: Overall converted GPA of 6.0 and a grade of at least 6.0 in Mathematics A to be assessed in quota 1.
Standby cut-off 2026: 10.1.
Quota 2 subjects: English B and Mathematics A.
Admission area number on optagelse.dk: 22118.

AU: "The international Bachelor's Degree Programme in Data Science has limited spots and is intended for international students. Applicants with Danish A are therefore advised to apply for the corresponding Danish-taught programme in Datavidenskab as their first priority."

programmes.name: IT Product Development
programmes.summary: Computer science oriented towards making things people use: designing, prototyping and evaluating digital products rather than only writing the code underneath. The entry requirements are identical to Computer Science, but the 2026 cut-off was more than a point lower and the standby cut-off much lower again, so it is the most reachable of AU's three English-taught computing degrees.
programmes.requirementsText: Specific admission requirements: You must fulfil the following specific admission requirements: English B. Mathematics A. B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade. Grade point Average (GPA) requirement of 6.0 in quota 1: You must have a minimum GPA of 6.0 and a minimum GPA of 6.0 in Mathematics A on the Danish 7-point grading scale in your qualifying examination to be assessed in quota 1.
extraRequirements: Overall converted GPA of 6.0 and a grade of at least 6.0 in Mathematics A to be assessed in quota 1.
Standby cut-off 2026: 6.9 — far below the quota 1 cut-off of 10.1, so ticking standby is worth doing here.
Quota 2 subjects: English B and Mathematics A.
Admission area number on optagelse.dk: 22128.
AU advises Danish applicants to also apply for the Danish-taught It-Produktudvikling.

programmes.name: Economics and Business Administration
programmes.summary: The standard Danish business economics degree taught in English: how a company's activities can be analysed and managed so they create value, and how to build strategies for growth. All teaching and all reading is in English because the programme is built around international business. It is the broadest of AU's English-taught degrees and the usual route into AU's business master's programmes.
programmes.requirementsText: Specific admission requirements: You must fulfil the following specific admission requirements: English B. Mathematics B. History B or History of Ideas B or Social Studies B or Contemporary History B or International Economics B. B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade. Grade point Average (GPA) requirement of 6.0 in quota 1: You must have a minimum GPA of 6.0 on the Danish 7-point grading scale in your qualifying examination to be assessed in quota 1.
extraRequirements: Converted-GPA floor of 6.0 to be assessed in quota 1.
Standby cut-off 2026: 8.6.
Quota 2 subjects: English B, Mathematics B, and History B or History of Ideas B or Social Studies B or Contemporary History B or International Economics B.
Admission area number on optagelse.dk: 22615.

programmes.name: Economics and Business Administration (Herning)
programmes.summary: The same subject as the Aarhus programme — how companies create value, attract customers and decide — taught on AU's small Herning campus in West Jutland, with a practical bent towards how businesses actually operate. Much lower cut-off than Aarhus, and a smaller, more personal setting; the trade-off is a town of about fifty thousand rather than Denmark's second city.
programmes.requirementsText: A qualifying examination as well as the following specific admission requirements (A, B and C refers to the subject level in the Danish upper secondary school with A being the highest level possible): English B. Mathematics B. History B or History of Ideas B or Contemporary History B or Social Science B or International Economics B. The admission requirements must be met and documented by 5 July in the year of application unless you apply for conditional admission.
extraRequirements: No 6.0 quota 1 GPA floor is stated for this programme, unlike the other five English-taught AU degrees.
Standby cut-off 2026: 6.0.
Quota 2 subjects: English B, Mathematics B, and History B or History of Ideas B or Social Science B or Contemporary History B or International Economics B.
Optional "meeting to match expectations" offered to everyone who applies in quota 2 by 15 March. It is not an interview and it is not assessed.
Admission area number on optagelse.dk: 22935.
